rv.q: But for such a starry cast Tamara Harvey’s production has a disappointing lack of sparkle. You do not feel the story’s charge, its complications around love and its stinging losses. The tone is too soft-edged, almost endearing, and the cast such an ensemble that there is no magnetic centre to hold you.

At least, I thought it would be, until two high-profile productions were announced to be gracing the stages of the UK this year. First up is the RSC, staging a new adaptation written by Laura Wade, whose previous RSC work (also directed by Tamara Harvey), The Constant Wife , was a tremendous hit.
